title: Camera angles
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:48Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Camera angles
card: The camera looks down on the subject. This can make the subject seem small, weak or less important.
The camera looks up at the subject. This can make the subject seem powerful, large or important.
The camera is level with the subject. This can make the subject feel equal to the viewer, as if they are on the same level.
Creators choose an angle to shape how we feel about a person or thing in an image. The angle is about where the camera sits, not how close the subject looks.
draft.remember: The angle of the camera can shape how we see a subject: looking down, looking up or level.

a.q: A photo of a lost puppy is taken from above, with the camera looking down at it. What effect does this angle most likely have?
opts: The puppy seems small and weak
The puppy seems powerful and large
The puppy seems equal to the viewer
The puppy seems close and personal
a.why: A high angle looks down on a subject, so it can make the subject seem small or weak. A low angle would make the puppy seem powerful. Close and personal describes how near the subject is, not the angle.
a.clue: Think about which way the camera is looking.

b.q: A poster for a school sports carnival shows the team captain photographed from near the ground, looking up at her. What is the poster most likely trying to make viewers feel about her?
opts: That she is strong and impressive
That she is shy and unsure
That she is just like any other student
That she is far away from the viewer
b.why: A low angle looks up at the subject, which can make her seem powerful and impressive. An eye level shot would suggest she is equal to the viewer. Being far away comes from how distant the shot is, not from the camera angle.
b.clue: Where is the camera compared with her face?

a.best: The puppy seems small and weak

b.best: That she is strong and impressive
